# SOP-P2-L3-05 Planned shutdown - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, EQ-P2-L3-IH03  
Related documents: ECN-2026-037, MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3, QS-PROC-10

1. Purpose and scope  
   1.1 Purpose: Define controlled steps for a planned shutdown of the Machining line to perform maintenance, inspection, and changeover tasks on EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03.  
   1.2 Scope: Applies to all maintenance, operations, and supervision personnel executing a planned shutdown on P2-L3 machining line. Follow referenced documents for change control, equipment maintenance history, and quality records.

2. Background and rationale  
   2.1 Background: Planned shutdowns reduce unplanned downtime and ensure safe access for maintenance on high-energy items and heat-treatment equipment. This SOP standardizes sequence and responsibilities to protect personnel and maintain material quality.  
   2.2 Rationale: Consistent shutdown sequencing prevents thermal shock, hydraulic damage, and material contamination. Specific setpoints and flows for heat-treat and induction equipment are maintained in this procedure to permit safe cooldown, purge, and reactivation steps.

3. Preconditions (step sequence must be verified before execution)  
   3.1 Authorization: Obtain written approval from the shift supervisor or maintenance planner before initiating shutdown. Authorization must reference ECN-2026-037.  
   3.2 Notifications: Operations control, quality, and safety must be notified and acknowledge the shutdown plan. Quality acknowledgement must reference QS-PROC-10 requirements for process control.  
   3.3 Lockout-tagout kits and permits must be available and matched to the equipment listed in this document. Refer to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for equipment-specific permits for EQ-P2-L3-IH03.  
   3.4 Materials staging: All billets and work-in-progress must be accounted for and routed per operations instructions before powerdown.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE) and access control  
   4.1 Required PPE: Hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, and heat-resistant gloves for anyone accessing hot surfaces. Respiratory protection as required by the local safety officer for any confined-space or fume risk.  
   4.2 Access control: Only authorized personnel listed on the permit may enter the work area. A single point of contact will maintain the access log for the duration of the shutdown.

5. Shutdown steps (numbered execution sequence)  
   5.1 Prepare control and safety documentation: Verify permits, isolation diagrams, and emergency procedures are present at the worksite. Confirm copies of ECN-2026-037 and MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 are available for reference.  
   5.2 Secure in-process material: Confirm removal or safe retention of all material on EQ-P2-L3-RR01 and associated conveyors. Record disposition in the shutdown log. Rationale: prevents material damage and contamination during maintenance. Example: move billets to the staging rack and tag locations.  
   5.3 Electrical isolation: Implement lockout-tagout on main feeds to EQ-P2-L3-RR01, EQ-P2-L3-HT02, and EQ-P2-L3-IH03. Verify zero energy at local test points. Record verifier name in the permit. Rationale: prevents accidental energization during maintenance.  
   5.4 Fluid and gas isolation: Close and tag supply valves to the heat-treat furnace and induction heater per procedure diagrams. Bleed residual pressure to a safe state as indicated on the permit. Record valve numbers and verifier initials in the work record.  
   5.5 Controlled cooldown for heat source equipment: Ensure staff understand that the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Rationale: awareness of the austenitizing setpoint is required to plan safe cooldown and avoid thermal shock to refractory and fixtures. Example: consult control logs before entering the furnace chamber for inspection.  
   5.6 Cooling water and circulation actions for induction heater: The coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min. Rationale: maintaining minimum flow prevents coil overheating and potential failure. Example: verify flow meter reading and document status in the equipment checklist before isolating cooling circuits.  
   5.7 Ventilation and purge: Purge confined or enclosed spaces per safety permit before entry. Maintain ventilation until fume and gas monitors show safe conditions. Record monitor readings in the shutdown log. Rationale: prevents exposure to combustion products and process fumes.  
   5.8 Mechanical isolation and securing: Install physical isolation blocks where required. Tag and document each isolation in the permit. Rationale: provides a secondary mechanical safeguard in addition to LOTO.  
   5.9 Maintenance and inspection tasks: Perform maintenance tasks as authorized. For EQ-P2-L3-IH03 consult MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 for component-level instructions. Record all replaced parts and observations in the maintenance record. Rationale: traceability and historical condition tracking. Example records: coil inspection notes, cooling circuit swab test results, and electrical connector torque checks (recorded only if torque values are in MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3).  
   5.10 Pre-energization checks: Complete the pre-start checklist and verify completion of corrective actions. Ensure quality representative signs off on any process-critical items per QS-PROC-10. Rationale: prevents reintroduction of defects into production.

6. Restart sequence and verification  
   6.1 Controlled restart: Follow pre-start checklist. Confirm that documented inspections and tests are complete and recorded. Do not reintroduce material until quality sign-off is recorded. Rationale: ensures process integrity and traceability.  
   6.2 Performance verification: Run operational checks and process verification per QS-PROC-10. Record results in the restart log.

7. Records to keep (minimum required)  
   7.1 Shutdown permit and LOTO verification signatures.  
   7.2 Equipment isolation log including valve and breaker identifiers and verifier initials.  
   7.3 Cooling water flow verification for EQ-P2-L3-IH03 with recorded statement that the coil cooling water flow minimum for Machining induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P2-L3-IH03) is 72 L/min.  
   7.4 Furnace control log showing awareness of the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C.  
   7.5 Maintenance actions and parts replaced, cross-referenced to MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3 where applicable.  
   7.6 Quality sign-off documents per QS-PROC-10 and any deviation records referencing ECN-2026-037.

8. Examples and common issues  
   8.1 Example: If cooling flow drops below acceptable level during pre-start check, tag equipment out of service and initiate corrective action; document actions and notify quality. Rationale: protects coil integrity and prevents scrap generation.  
   8.2 Common issue: Incomplete isolation of auxiliary circuits—mitigation: follow the isolation checklist and obtain two-person verification.

9. Roles and responsibilities  
   9.1 Maintenance lead: Execute LOTO, perform maintenance, and complete records.  
   9.2 Operations lead: Ensure safe material disposition and support restart verification.  
   9.3 Quality representative: Verify process-critical items and sign off per QS-PROC-10.  
   9.4 Safety officer: Approve permits and verify PPE and atmospheric testing.

10. Sign-off (to be completed at job close)  
   10.1 Maintenance lead name and signature: __________________________________  
   10.2 Operations lead name and signature: __________________________________  
   10.3 Quality representative name and signature (QS-PROC-10): __________________________________  
   10.4 Safety officer name and signature: __________________________________

References: ECN-2026-037, MM-P2-L3-IH03-S3, QS-PROC-10
